focus: 장 is the counter for flat things (photos, tickets, paper) – a real counter-word trap, but the worked example 백 장 lacks romanization.
N보다 (더) = 'more than N' comparative; salvage that one rule alone – the tip jams in (으)로 as a second rule and leaves 카메라보다 더 자주 unromanized.
-(으)러 + motion verb = 'go (somewhere) in order to do'; keep the romanized example but romanize the cited 가다/다니다.
-(으)면 = 'if' conditional attached to the verb; real rule, but the quoted 날씨가 좋으면 is only partially romanized (joeumyeon covers one word).
KakaoTalk is Korea's default messenger and gets verbified – 카톡하다 = 'to text'; romanize 카톡해요.
쓰다 means both 'use' and 'write' – a one-word-two-meanings landmine; romanize the worked example 이모티콘을 써요.
-아/어 놓다 marks a state you set up and leave in place (phone left on silent); cut the second rule (N 중에) and romanize fully.
다 before a verb = 'completely/all' – 다 썼어요 is 'used it all up'; a reusable pattern, but 데이터를 다 썼어요 needs full romanization.
다 되다 = 'be all done/used up' is the everyday way to say something died or ran out; romanize the whole quoted phrase including 배터리가.
못 = 'can't' (inability), distinct from plain 안 negation; real rule but the worked example 로그인을 못 했어요 lacks romanization.
꺼지다 = 'turn off by itself' – the intransitive counterpart of 끄다 (turn it off); make the pair explicit and romanize the example.
Sound 'comes out' in Korean – 소리가 나다, so 'no sound' is 소리가 안 나요; romanize the negative example too.
-비 is a productive suffix meaning 'fee/cost' (수리비, 택시비) – reusable pattern; romanize the sibling example 택시비.
-게 turns adjectives into adverbs (길게 = 'long', so 길게 누르다 = long-press); romanize the worked example 길게 눌러요.
Noun + 때 = 'at the time of / during' (세일 때 = during the sale); romanize the worked example.
Honored subjects (grandma) take the honorific -(으)시-/-세요 on the verb; real register rule but 할머니는 is unromanized.
노트북 means laptop, not a paper notebook (that's 공책) – a genuine Konglish false friend; romanize 공책.
켜지다 = 'turn on by itself' – intransitive counterpart of 켜다 (turn it on), so 안 켜져요 = it won't come on; romanize the example.
Seollal follows the lunar calendar (음력), so it is not January 1 – real cultural logic; romanize 설날.
Age is 'eaten' in Korean – 나이를 먹다; eating tteokguk adds a year. Romanize 한 살 더 먹어요 and drop the nested quotes.
께 is the honorific 'to' (replacing 에게) for elders; romanize the worked example 어른들께.
드리다 is the humble 'give' used toward elders; romanize the worked example 세배를 드려요.
Sebaetdon comes after the sebae bow, not before – order-of-ritual logic; romanize 세배.
Other people's feelings take -어하다 (기쁘다 → 기뻐하다) – a classic trap; romanize 아이들이 in the example.
팔리다 = 'get sold', the -리- passive of 팔다 – say it in plain words and romanize 팔다.
Number + -이나 stresses the amount is a lot ('a full five hours'); romanize the worked example 다섯 시간이나.
햇- is a productive prefix meaning 'this year's first harvest of' a food; romanize the full worked example 햇곡식.
Dates use Sino-Korean numerals – 오월 팔일 = May 8; make the numeral-system point the one rule and romanize the date.
V-아/어 드리다 = do something FOR an elder, the humble version of -아/어 주다; generalize the pattern beyond the single gloss.
Remembering happens TO you in Korean – 생각나다 = the thought 'comes up' by itself, not 'I think of'; sharpen the contrast and romanize fully.
생일 축하해요 is the standard polite birthday formula; replace the linguistics term 해요체 with plain words (or romanize it).
환갑 – the milestone 60th-birthday celebration; romanize 예순 살 and keep it to that one cultural fact.
-마다 = 'every', attaching directly to a noun (생일마다 = every birthday); romanize the worked example.
